data.current_description: `autonomy` governs OUTBOUND: auto sends, notify sends and files a notice, approve_first holds for a human. `inbound_jobs_on` governs INBOUND and is the one people trip over: it defaults to `fresh` (uncorrelated mail only), so REPLIES to mail you sent do not wake a job. Any support or reply-driven workflow wants `all`.
data.summary_suggestion: Update inbox autonomy and inbound job settings
data.description_suggestion: Updates an inbox's configuration, specifically its autonomy and inbound job handling. `autonomy` controls outbound behavior: `auto` sends immediately, `notify` sends and files a notice, `approve_first` holds for human approval. `inbound_jobs_on` controls which inbound messages trigger jobs: `fresh` (default) processes only uncorrelated mail (not replies to sent messages), while `all` processes all messages including replies. Returns the updated inbox object.
data.reasoning: Original summary is too generic. Description is detailed but poorly structured and uses unexplained jargon. Improved summary is more specific about what is being updated. Improved description reorganizes the information into clear sections for each setting, explains the default behavior, and indicates what is returned.

data.current_description: 202 with `status`. `sent` went to SES; `pending_approval` means the inbox holds agent mail for a human and NOTHING has been delivered yet; `scheduled` will send later. `reply_to` states which address replies go to and WHY — `relay_fallback` means the branded domain cannot yet receive, so correlation runs over the relay instead. `suppressed` lists recipients dropped because they bounced, complained or opted out.
data.summary_suggestion: Send a message from an inbox
data.description_suggestion: Sends a message from the specified inbox. Returns 202 with a status object indicating delivery state: `sent` (delivered to SES), `pending_approval` (held for human approval—not yet delivered), or `scheduled` (will send later). Includes `reply_to` address and reason (e.g., `relay_fallback` if the branded domain cannot receive, so replies route through the relay). The `suppressed` field lists recipients dropped due to bounces, complaints, or opt-outs. Partial failures are reported per-recipient.
